note: Page configuration, not a record. The proof strip on the home page and the lab on a page (lab launch, 2026-10-24). Claim texts hold no digits and no number words; each {name} is a value read from the cited experiment record by a JSON pointer (scripts/lab-pages.mjs renderLabProof) and linked to it, and the build checks the rendered strip with scripts/number-provenance.mjs. A claim's record must be a measured experiment record with a decided verdict (briefProblems refuses the router-arm records). Brokers appear by the letters their published records use; no provider is named. Plain-language home (2026-11-16): each claim also carries a `limit` in words, shown under it as "Limit:" on the home and the lab on a page; a limit, like a text, holds no digit and no number word, and every claim on this list must have one.

claims.headline: The cheapest reviewer caught {cheapCaught} of {cheapOf} planted defects
claims.text: It cost {cheapCost} per review. The most expensive cost {dearCost} and caught {dearCaught} of {dearOf}. Their uncertainty ranges overlapped.
claims.provenance: On clean changes, the cheapest reviewer raised {cheapFA} false alarms in {cheapClean} reviews and the most expensive raised {dearFA} in {dearClean}.
claims.limit: Repeat runs on private changes with planted defects. A catch meant flagging the right file.

claims.headline: Reseller prices differed by {spreadS}
claims.text: Across {calls} requests, resellers A and C billed list price and B billed more for the same models. Every successful response reported the requested model.
claims.limit: Prices cover billed calls during the test window. Some requests failed.

claims.headline: Self-check cleared {clearedA} of {flaggedA} flagged reviews
claims.text: In the repeat, it cleared {clearedB} of {flaggedB}. With {faA} and {faB} false alarms left, the study’s answer on adopting the extra check was {decision}.
claims.limit: We scored verdicts on private changes. We did not check the model’s explanations.
